records.also_known_as: IRD / ACC PAYE Earners' Levy rate & maximum covered salary cap (2026/27)
records.topic: ACC levy, high-income cap & mortgage servicing
records.latest_value: $156,641 max covered earnings | $1.75/$100 levy | $125,313/yr max 80% ACC payout
records.source_full: Accident Compensation (Earners' Levy) Regulations & Inland Revenue PAYE Schedule (2026/27)
records.source_series_ids: ACC Earners' Levy Rate & Maximum Liable Earnings Threshold
records.data_type: Public-domain statutory levy/cap & HLF-calculated 80% gross compensation ceiling
records.definition: The statutory ACC Earners' Levy rate deducted from employee PAYE wages, the maximum liable earnings cap, and the resulting maximum 80% gross weekly compensation payable by ACC.
records.official_data: ACC / IRD 2026/27 Statutory Schedule: Earners' levy = $1.75 per $100 incl. GST ($1.52 excl. GST); Maximum liable earnings = $156,641 (vs $152,790 in 2025/26).
records.hlf_interpretation: HLF market context: This affects borrowers in two ways: (1) In mortgage servicing calculators, the 1.75% ACC levy reduces net take-home pay on earnings up to $156,641; and (2) For an eligible accident, ACC caps income replacement at 80% of earnings up to $156,641 ($125,313/yr gross)—leaving higher-income earners with a larger percentage drop in income, and self-employed company owners splitting shareholder salaries potentially under-covered unless structured via ACC CoverPlus Extra or private cover.
records.methodology: Published by ACC and Inland Revenue under statutory regulations for the tax year commencing 1 April 2026 ($1.75 per $100 of liable earnings incl. GST; maximum liable earnings of $156,641).
records.historical_data_from: ACC & IRD statutory earners' levy schedule (2024/25–2026/27)

CC BY 4.0.
records.summary_text: For the 2026/27 tax year, the statutory ACC Earners' Levy is $1.75 per $100 (1.75% incl. GST) (up from $1.67 in 2025/26) up to a Maximum Liable Earnings cap of $156,641 (up from $152,790, for a maximum annual levy of $2,741.22)—setting ACC's maximum 80% weekly compensation ceiling at an HLF-derived $125,312.80/year ($2,409.86/week gross).

records.name: ACC annual injury claims vs weekly income compensation claims (accident vs illness scope)
records.also_known_as: ACC Annual Report total claims vs weekly compensation claims
records.latest_value: 105,000 weekly compensation claims (5.0% of 2,100,000+ ACC injury claims)
records.change: -2,000 weekly compensation claims (-1.9% YoY) | ACC covers accidental injury (generally not non-injury illness)
records.source_full: Accident Compensation Corporation (ACC) — Annual Report (2025/26)
records.source_series_ids: ACC Total Registered Claims & Weekly Compensation Entitlement Claims
records.data_type: Officially reported ACC claim counts/costs & HLF-derived weekly compensation share
records.definition: The annual number of new injury claims registered with ACC across New Zealand versus the number of claims receiving weekly income compensation for time off work.
records.official_data: ACC Annual Report (2025/26): Total accepted injury claims = 2,100,000+ (+1.6% YoY); New weekly compensation claims = 105,000 (-1.9% from 107,000 in 2024/25).
records.hlf_calculation: 105,000 weekly compensation claims ÷ 2,100,000 total accepted injury claims = 5.0%
records.formula: Weekly Compensation Share = (105,000 Weekly Compensation Claims ÷ 2,100,000 Total Accepted Claims) × 100 = 5.0%
records.hlf_interpretation: HLF market context: Only 5.0% of accepted ACC claims involve weekly income compensation. Under the Accident Compensation Act 2001, ACC covers physical injuries caused by an accident (plus narrow statutory categories such as work-related gradual-process conditions, treatment injuries, and certain mental injuries), and generally does not cover non-injury illness (such as cancer, heart attack, stroke, or degenerative illness)—which is the gap addressed by private Income Protection, Mortgage Repayment, and Trauma insurance.
records.methodology: Sourced from ACC's Annual Report covering accepted injury claims, treatment/rehabilitation expenditure, and weekly compensation entitlements.
records.citation: HLF Pulse, Home Loan Factory. "ACC annual injury claims vs weekly income compensation claims (accident vs illness scope)," 2025/26 ACC Financial Year. Derived by HLF from Accident Compensation Corporation (ACC) — Annual Report (2025/26). https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/acc-weekly-compensation-claims/ (checked 10 November 2026). CC BY 4.0.
records.summary_text: In the 2025/26 financial year, ACC accepted over 2,100,000 new injury claims across New Zealand (up 1.6% year-on-year), of which 105,000 claims—an HLF-derived 5.0% share (down 1.9% from 107,000 in 2024/25)—received weekly income compensation for time off work alongside $5.0B+ in treatment and rehabilitation support.

records.name: Average gross borrower income on approved FHB mortgage applications
records.also_known_as: RBNZ C41 Borrower Gross Income (BGI) — First-home buyer mean application income
records.source_full: Reserve Bank of New Zealand Table C41
records.source_series_ids: DTINI.MPA (Borrower Gross Income by TDTI band)
records.data_type: HLF-calculated mean gross income across C41 TDTI bands (Total band income ÷ implied borrower count)
records.definition: The HLF-calculated mean annual pre-tax gross income across approved New Zealand first-home buyer mortgage applications (combining all single and joint applicants on the loan).
records.official_data: RBNZ Table C41 (September 2026) Official FHB Band Averages: TDTI ≤ 3x income: $197,000 | 3x < TDTI ≤ 4x income: $151,000 | 4x < TDTI ≤ 5x income: $139,000 | 5x < TDTI ≤ 6x income: $125,000 | TDTI > 6x income: $123,000.
records.hlf_calculation: Total band gross income ÷ implied borrower count across C41 TDTI bands = $144,232 (FHB)
records.formula: Total Gross Income NZDm across all C41 TDTI bands ÷ Implied Borrower Count (Sum of [Band NZDm ÷ Band Avg Income NZD000s])
records.hlf_interpretation: HLF market context: RBNZ Table C41 publishes band-level figures rather than a single nationwide mean; the overall figure is calculated by HLF. Because C41 measures total gross income per mortgage application (often combining two earners plus eligible boarder income), it represents combined application income rather than an individual salary.
records.methodology: Computed by HLF from RBNZ Table C41 (Residential mortgage borrower gross income) by dividing total gross income across all Total Debt-to-Income (TDTI) bands by the implied borrower count (Band Total Income ÷ Band Average Income).
records.citation: HLF Pulse, Home Loan Factory. "Average gross borrower income on approved FHB mortgage applications," September 2026. Derived by HLF from Reserve Bank of New Zealand Table C41. https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/borrower-income/ (checked 10 November 2026). CC BY 4.0.
records.summary_text: Based on HLF's calculation across RBNZ Table C41's five Debt-to-Income bands (total band gross income divided by implied borrower count), approved New Zealand first-home buyer mortgage applications averaged $144,232 in gross borrower income in September 2026 (with official RBNZ band averages ranging from $123,000 to $197,000).

records.source_full: Reserve Bank of New Zealand Table C40

records.definition: The HLF-derived percentage of total new first-home buyer mortgage lending committed at a Total Debt-to-Income (TDTI) ratio above 6x gross income in RBNZ Table C40, compared against the 20% RBNZ speed-limit threshold.
